title: Hans Zimmer Is Bringing ‘The Next Level’ Live Show Back to North America in 2027
summary: The Oscar & Grammy winner will take his cinematic catalog to arenas across the U.S. and Canada, with stops in Los Angeles, New York, Chicago and more.
contentText:
Hans Zimmer is bringing his blockbuster movie scores back to the stage.

The Oscar- and Grammy winning composer announced Thursday (Sept. 17) that he will be returning to North America in 2027 with Hans Zimmer Lice — The Next Level, bringing his latest live production to arenas across the U.S and Canada.

Hans Zimmer’s ‘Next Level’ Tour Is Heading Down Under

The 32-date run kicks off Feb. 17 at PeoplesBank Arena in Hartford, Connecticut, before making stops in New York, Philadelphia, Boston, Chicago, Atlanta, Miami, Denver and Los Angeles. The tour wraps April 11 at Portland, Oregon’s Moda Center.

The North American dates follow Zimmer’s European run of  The Next Level , which ranked among the top 10 worldwide tours during the first half of 2026. The production features Zimmer performing with a 19-piece ensemble, with the show built around a combination of live instrumentation, electronic elements and large-scale visuals.

“I want fans to feel like they’re at a rave party or riding a roller coaster,” Zimmer said in a statement provided to Billboard . “For me, every show is a new voyage of discovery.”

The composer has spent decades creating the musical identities of some of Hollywood’s biggest films, from  The Lion King  and  Gladiator  to  The Dark Knight  trilogy,  Inception ,  Interstellar  and Denis Villeneuve’s  Dune  films. His résumé also includes  Pirates of the Caribbean ,  Man of Steel ,  Wonder Woman ,  Dunkirk ,  No Time to Die  and  Top Gun: Maverick .

Zimmer’s live shows allow for these compositions to exist in a different life, making music originally written to accompany scenes on screen into the centerpiece of a full-scale arena production.  The Next Level  is the latest addition to his touring schedule, which has famously taken him to arenas around the world.

And there’s more Zimmer on the big screen ahead: He is set to return as composer for the third installment of Villeneuve’s  Dune  franchise, currently slated for release Dec. 18.
